subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — indemnity & defense control

Subject: MSA redlines — indemnity (IP) and Order Form questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. Attached are the redlines Solstice legal put together for the MSA and the Order Form (see Solstice_MSA_Redlines.docx and OrderForm_Solstice_v3.pdf). Two high-priority asks from our end:

1) Broad customer indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from model outputs — we need Redwood to defend and indemnify Solstice where customer usage of generated content allegedly infringes a third party.
2) Defense control & counsel selection — Solstice would like joint approval of outside counsel and an explicit process for settlement approval.

We appreciate earlier conversations about limiting scope for training-data claims; however, our procurement team is concerned about downstream risk and wants broader protection tied to the Order Form’s production environment.

Can Redwood provide a commercial proposal (cap, proof of insurance, and any carveouts) so we can move to internal signoff this month? Also flagging timing constraints — our security and procurement teams expect an answer by end of day Friday PST to keep the Q1 PO.

Attachments: [Attachment: Solstice_MSA_Redlines.docx (docx, 42KB)], [Attachment: OrderForm_Solstice_v3.pdf (pdf, 78KB)]

Best,
Maya Singh

Maya — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Ben (Sales) to lead a joint commercial/legal response.

High-level next steps from our side:
- Kimberly will review the redlines and propose a limited counter that protects Solstice for third-party claims that directly result from Redwood’s service defects (e.g., mis-delivery, contaminated model assets), while preserving Redwood’s carveouts for claims based on customer prompts or customer-provided data.
- Ben will put together a commercial package (insurance evidence, proposed cap, and an optional limited settlement escrow).

We’ll target a formal written counter by Thu 03/04 PST to respect your Friday timeline. If we need faster escalation, I can route to our VP Legal.

Naomi
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, Maya Singh <maya.singh@solsticelabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — indemnity (IP) and Order Form questions

Maya / Naomi / Ben — I reviewed Solstice’s redlines and sketched a focused counterproposal (attached: Redwood_Countertrack_changes.docx). Summary of our legal position and compromise suggestions: 

1) Scope of indemnity: Redwood can agree to indemnify Solstice for third-party claims alleging that Redwood-provided models or model outputs infringe third-party intellectual property, but only where:
   - the claim arises from a Redwood-hosted model variant delivered under the signed Order Form (i.e., not self-hosted or modified customer model), AND
   - Solstice’s use conforms with Redwood’s published usage policies and reasonably disclosed prompt examples, AND
   - Solstice provides prompt notice and reasonably cooperates in defense.

2) Carveouts we must keep: claims arising from customer prompts or customer-supplied data, customer modifications of model outputs, or customer-hosted derivatives. This preserves predictable risk for Redwood given the open-ended nature of generated outputs.

3) Defense control & counsel: Redwood requests right to control defense with the option to propose counsel; Solstice may retain independent counsel at its own cost if there is a material conflict. For settlements that impose money damages on Redwood, Redwood’s prior written consent will be required (we propose a commercially reasonable multi-step approval process).

4) Caps & insurance: propose a mutual cap tied to the annual contract value (ACV) — Redwood suggests 2x ACV for IP indemnity with an absolute carveout for punitive or intentional misconduct. We will supply current commercial liability insurance declarations and can consider an escrow mechanism for exceptional claims.

5) Transitional protection: For claims related to model updates, we propose a 120-day window post-deployment where Redwood will assume defense obligations for regression-level infringement claims attributable to our model change.

If Solstice needs broader customer-side indemnity (i.e., defending the customer for downstream uses), that materially increases Redwood’s exposure and would need insurance and pricing adjustments; Ben — please advise commercial delta.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_Countertrack_changes.docx (docx, 28KB)]

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Maya Singh <maya.singh@solsticelabs.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — indemnity (IP) and Order Form questions

Maya / Team — quick commercial note to make tradeoffs explicit:

Option A (Standard): Redwood accepts Kimberly’s limited indemnity scope. No price change. Redwood provides proof of insurance (CGL and tech E&O) and offers a 2x ACV cap.

Option B (Expanded customer defense): Redwood will expand to defend named Solstice customers for downstream claims only if Solstice: (i) agrees to a 4x ACV price uplift; (ii) adds Solstice as an additional insured; and (iii) accepts a running limitation that excludes claims arising from customer prompts. This also requires underwriter signoff.

Given Solstice’s timeline, Option A is easiest to accept quickly; Option B is an executive decision and would add 2–3 weeks for procurement and underwriting.

If you confirm Option A, we’ll prepare the redline-ready Order Form and route a DocuSign for signature.

Thanks — Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
